title: Impulse and force–time graphs; Work done; Kinetic and potential energy; conservation; Work–energy theorem and dissipative forces; Power and efficiency
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: E02-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; E02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; E01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; D10-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D10-1#N.12, E01-1#N.5, E02-1#N.4a, E03-1#N.15, E04-1#N.3, E01-1#N.9b, E02-1#N.10a, E04-1#N.6b, E02-1#N.12, E04-1#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mechanical energy
items.clue: Sum that stays constant when there is no friction or drag.

items.label: Gravitational potential energy
items.clue: Store that depends on position, lost as a dropped ball speeds up.

items.label: Component
items.clue: Part of a force along the displacement: the only part that transfers energy.

items.label: Crumple zone
items.clue: Car feature that lengthens the stopping time, making the average force smaller.

questions.stem: Two identical 0.50 kg gliders on an air track each move at 2.0 m s⁻¹ towards an obstacle. Glider 1 hits a steel buffer and bounces straight back at 2.0 m s⁻¹; the contact lasts 0.010 s. Glider 2 hits a foam pad and stops; the contact lasts 0.040 s. How many times larger is the average force on glider 1 than the average force on glider 2?

options.text: 1, as both gliders arrive with the same speed

questions.stem: A worker uses a rope to lower a box straight down at constant speed. Which statement about the work done on the box during the descent is correct?

options.text: The tension does positive work and gravity does negative work on the box.
The tension does negative work and gravity does positive work.
The tension and gravity both do positive work on the box as it moves.
Neither force does any work, as the box's speed does not change.

questions.stem: Object A has mass m and moves at speed 2v. Object B has mass 2m and moves at speed v. What is the kinetic energy of object A divided by the kinetic energy of object B?

options.text: ½

questions.explanation: A: ½m(2v)² = 2mv². B: ½(2m)v² = mv². So A has twice B's kinetic energy: doubling the speed multiplies it by 4, doubling the mass only by 2.

questions.stem: Motor A raises a 200 N load through 3.0 m in 6.0 s. Motor B raises a 100 N load through 6.0 m in 4.0 s. Both lift at constant speed. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A develops more power, as it lifts the heavier load.
B does more work, as it lifts its load twice as high.
Both do equal work, and B develops more power.
Both develop equal power, as they do equal work.

questions.explanation: Each does 600 J (200 × 3.0 and 100 × 6.0). B does it in less time: 600 ÷ 4.0 = 150 W against 600 ÷ 6.0 = 100 W.

questions.stem: A child on a toboggan slides across level snow. The child and toboggan have a total mass of 50 kg and slow down from 8.0 m s⁻¹ to 6.0 m s⁻¹. What is the magnitude of the net work done on the child–toboggan system during this time?

A student carries a bag of weight 15 N up a flight of stairs at constant velocity. The bag moves 4.0 m horizontally and rises 3.0 m, so it travels 5.0 m along the stairs. How much work does the student's upward force do on the bag?

options.text: 60 J, the upward force multiplied by the horizontal distance.
45 J, the upward force multiplied by the height gained.
75 J, the upward force multiplied by the distance along the stairs.
Zero, as the bag moves at constant velocity, so no work is done on it.

questions.explanation: The force is vertical and the displacement is 5.0 m at an angle θ to it, with cos θ = 3.0/5.0. Work = 15 × 5.0 × 0.60 = 45 J: the force times the 3.0 m rise.

questions.stem: A spring of spring constant 250 N m⁻¹ is compressed by 0.080 m and then released. It launches a block of mass 0.40 kg along a smooth horizontal track. All the elastic potential energy becomes the block's kinetic energy. What is the speed of the block?

options.text: 7.1 m s⁻¹
2.0 m s⁻¹
2.8 m s⁻¹
1.4 m s⁻¹

questions.stem: A skier of mass 60 kg starts from rest at the top of a slope and descends through a vertical height of 20 m. At the bottom her speed is 16 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the total work done on the skier by friction and air resistance during the descent?

Three identical stones are thrown from the top of a sea cliff with the same speed: one straight up, one horizontally and one straight down. Air resistance is negligible. Which stone hits the sea with the greatest speed?

options.text: The one thrown straight down, as its velocity starts in the direction of gravity.
The one thrown upwards, as it falls back from a greater height than the others.
The one thrown horizontally, as it keeps its horizontal speed while gaining vertical speed.
All land at equal speeds: same starting kinetic energy, same drop in height.

questions.explanation: Initial kinetic energy + potential energy lost = final kinetic energy, and both terms are equal for all three stones. The speeds are equal; only the directions and times of flight differ.

questions.stem: A block on a level, frictionless surface is sped up by a constant horizontal force. The work needed to speed the block up from rest to speed v is W. How many times W is needed to speed the block up from v to 3v?
